passage: Under the neem tree, the men of the family gathered to fix the water rota for the fields. Everyone waited for Nilesh to object, as he always did. Jagdish, an older cousin, had even folded both arms. But Nilesh, who had argued at every meeting since he was sixteen, said quietly, “The rota is fair. I only ask that the tractor be shared on Thursday, since my plot floods.” Nobody answered at first. An uncle muttered, “What has happened to him?” Jagdish unfolded both arms. Nilesh's mother, at the edge of the courtyard with the tea, said nothing but poured Nilesh's cup first. The next month, when Nilesh did object once, the others listened.

qa.q: Where did the men of the family gather to fix the water rota?
qa.a: They gathered under the neem tree.

qa.q: Why was the family surprised when Nilesh said the rota was fair?
qa.a: They expected him to object as he always did, since he had argued at every meeting since he was sixteen.

qa.q: What helped the family accept the change in Nilesh over time?
qa.a: Nilesh stayed calm and consistent, making one small request, and the following month, when he objected once, the others listened.

qa.q: What might Nilesh's mother have felt when she poured his cup first?
qa.a: Nilesh's mother seems quietly proud and supportive, backing him without words while the others were still unsure.

grounding: A young man quietly stops playing the family rebel, and the family resists at first and then adjusts to steady consistency.
